chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Jamhour, from Idrees ibn Yusuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut the bread with the knife, but break it with the hand, and let your breaking be opposite to that of the non-Arabs'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding breaking bread with hands versus cutting it with a knife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* emphasizes the etiquette of breaking bread by hand to distinguish Muslim practice from that of the Persians (al-Ajam), reflecting a broader Shia emphasis on *furqan* (differentiation) in daily customs. Scholars note that this simple act serves as a subtle marker of identity and adherence to the Sunnah, reinforcing communal unity through shared physical rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Idrees Bin Yusuf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘do not cut the bread with the knife, but break it with the hand, and let your breaking be opposite to that of the non-Arabs’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Idris ibn Yusuf who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Do not cut bread with knife but break it with your hand and others must break it for you. You must do the opposite of al-‘Ajam (non- Arabs).”’
